newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Foreign funds fuel Singapore shares to a firm end.
newsitem.headline: Foreign funds fuel Singapore shares to a firm end.

text.p: A spate of buying by European fund managers, notably in banking stocks, lifted the Singapore share market to a firmer close on Thursday, dealer said.
"European fund managers are buying all of the banks like DBS Foreign, OCBC, UOB Foreign and OUB Foreign," a dealer said.

"However, it's difficult to say whether this means there is further potential upside for this market," he said, adding that the near-term direction hinged on what U.S. policy-makers decide during next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"If the Fed does not hike rates, the STII is poised for further upside. We may see it test 2,250," another broker said.

The key Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended near its intraday high, at 2,206.09, up 23.78 points or 1.09 percent. Volume was moderate, around 119 million shares, with gainers leading losers by 189 to 122.
Dealers said most of the activity centred on blue-chips or index-linked stocks. Leading the actives were SingTel with 8.9 million shares and UOB Foreign with 3.6 million.
They said SingTel rebounded after failing to break support at S$3.00 (US$2.13) to close at S$3.16, up six cents.
CityDev was among the losers, shedding S$0.20 to end at S$12.00. US$1=S$1.41
